neighbours.label: A real word wrongly used where a similar-looking or similar-sounding verb belongs: ' ware' for wear, ' suite' for suit, ' beings' for begins, ' where' for were; the same words used correctly are quiet
fire: On Sundays the women would ware long white dresses to church.
The dry climate did not suite her, and she moved back north.
When the bell rings the crowd beings to move toward the gates.
The teachers at my old school where always kind to us.
Soldiers had to ware heavy boots even in the summer heat.
City life does not suite everyone, as my uncle found out.
Each spring the river beings to rise as the snow melts.
My grandparents where farmers in a valley near the border.
quiet: On Sundays the women would wear long white dresses to church.
The dry climate did not suit her, and she moved back north.
When the bell rings the crowd begins to move toward the gates.
The teachers at my old school were always kind to us.
We booked a large suite on the top floor of the hotel.
Human beings have lived in this valley for ten thousand years.
I do not know where the farmers sell their grain.
The shop sells kitchen ware and garden tools.

notes: Card: ware (wear), suite (suit), beings (begins), where (were), quite. Probes: ware 0.67, suite 0.65, beings 0.66, where 0.35; correct 'hotel suite' 0.01, 'human beings' 0.01, wear/suit 0.00. Partly general: brake(break) 0.23, bare(bear) 0.20, loose(lose) 0.18, but then/weather/form/desert/your/past ~0.00-0.04, so mainly these verbs.
